note: Why a column shows rock (the crust's bare-stone setting, riven-surface.json); the blocks every setting lays are in riven-surface.json. Certified rocky formations expose vanilla stone and resolve actual solid/void occupancy before fluids and cover. Their admission excludes supplied water and bank/inlet skirts. Authorized sediment replaces deposited volume and surface soil with sand. Earlier marine ownership and water heads remain unchanged; final authorized emergence is separate. Other exposed-stone rules retain precedence over dryland cover; deep general surface, yardang, cold-region and volcanic cuts expose stone. Earlier supplied water and wetland cover keep priority. Geometry supplies no ice, lava, new water, heat or reconstructed geological materials. Soil before rock (v90): a rocky shore shows rock only within splashBlocks of the water (plus capeSplashBlocks at full cape exposure) and on cliff faces within cliffFaceBlocks; inland of that it takes the ordinary cover. High ground shows rock above a treeline: the stone line (stoneAboveReference) at referenceCelsius, moved blocksPerDegree per degree of the column's temperature, at most lowestBelowStoneBlocks lower and highestAboveStoneBlocks higher; mountain landforms show rock only within mountainBelowTreelineBlocks of it. A cut shows rock when deeper than exposedCutDepthBlocks where nothing grows back, rising to growingCutBlocks where plants return: as moisture climbs moistureSpan past an aridity threshold (aridMoisture, plus aridMoisturePerDegreeAbove10 per degree above 10 C) and temperature through celsiusRange. Materials follow form (v150, form): each dry land column reads its 8 neighbours (their ground, or the water over it) at its spacing (one block in native cubes and fine preview cells, a coarser preview cell's width there): its largest fall and its slope over that 3 x 3 stencil (a Sobel gradient, steady on a staircase whose single falls alternate), both in blocks per block. From a fall of steps.thinFromFall its top lies directly on rock. It is part of a rock face, bare rock without snow, where it falls at least face.fromFall and its slope reaches face.fromSlope, that threshold raised and lowered by face.dither.share of a world-aligned value noise of face.dither.wavelengthBlocks (fineWeight of it from a second octave of fineWavelengthBlocks), so a face's edges form ragged patches. Its soil depth (blocks, counting the top) is the climate's: thinBlocks to thickBlocks as moisture rises from dryMoisture to wetMoisture, with coldShare of that rise in the cold and the rest as temperature at the column's height rises from coldCelsius to warmCelsius; less blocksLostPerSlope per block of slope (the larger of its stencil slope and its broad slope), plus blocksPerBlock of its curvature (its height below the mean of a world-aligned latticeBlocks lattice around it, within limitBlocks), times its ground rock's factor, within maximumBlocks. Below bareBelowBlocks (dithered as the face) the ground is bare rock; a grus rock below grusBelowBlocks shows gravel; the soil layer under the top is the depth less its top, rounded, within soilLayersMaximum. A step or bare ground above the snowline holds a snow block over rock, and a rock face none; ground facing north (rising toward +Z) is snowy up to northFacingCelsius warmer, in full from a rise of northFullFromSlope. Where it would be snowy (or in a frozen climate), ground that falls and whose slope reaches snow.shedFromSlope (dithered as the face) sheds its snow: it is a rock face.
